version.changelog: Simplify the login instructions to the code flow (maton login prints a link; finish with maton login --code <CODE>), drop the API Key subsection, and pin the Maton CLI install to 0.4.0.

llm.summary: This is a disclosed Monday.com automation skill that can access and change business data through Maton, but its sensitive actions are described and approval-gated.

dimensions.detail: Bash and network access are proportionate for CLI/API usage, and the raw API-key path is documented as a fallback with clear handling limits.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a pinned Maton CLI via npm or Homebrew, with optional pinned SDK packages; the artifact itself is Markdown-only and contains no embedded executable scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions repeatedly default to read/list calls, require explicit approval for new connections, writes, deployments, trigger destinations, and local event execution, and warn that fetched app content is untrusted.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: OAuth tokens, hosted functions, triggers, destinations, and event-watch checkpoints can persist beyond one session, but the skill discloses these effects and requires user-directed approval and cleanup guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill’s Monday.com GraphQL access, board/item mutations, hosted functions, triggers, and destinations match its stated purpose of managing and automating Monday.com workflows, including disclosed high-impact operations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Use this only if you trust Maton with your Monday.com account. Prefer OAuth over long-lived API keys, grant the narrowest scopes available, and carefully review any approval request for writes, deletions, hosted functions, triggers, or destinations, especially anything that forwards data to a third-party URL.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: The appendix wording about omitting request bodies or using PUT/DELETE is inconsistent with the skill’s main Monday.com POST-only GraphQL guidance, but it appears to be a documentation error in a fallback section, not hidden or malicious behavior.
[SDI-4] expected: The functions and triggers sections do add Maton automation capabilities, but the artifact explains that distinction, limits the Monday.com API surface, and gives approval and containment rules for persistent automation.
